findings.problem: The two dark column capitals behind (second and fourth columns from the left) still have paired heads with long upright ears and no horns, so they read as donkeys, not bulls.
findings.fix: On the two dark charcoal capitals of the second and fourth columns from the left, behind the gold ones, redraw each pair of animal heads as bulls like the gold capitals in front: short curved horns, small ears set sideways under the horns, broad muzzles, in the same dark charcoal and plum. Change nothing else.

findings.problem: Seven men and seven shields but only five spearheads (about six shafts): two men's fists hold nothing, the count error the earlier edit was meant to fix.
findings.fix: Rewrite the prompt for four spearmen, one spear each (the generator miscounts above four), and redraw.

findings.problem: Four men but five spearheads: one short spear's head sits beside the second man's face.
findings.fix: Redraw used; the editor can't change a count. Every man now grips a shaft and the spear wall reads at card size.

findings.problem: The trees' reflections run past the lake's blue onto bare paper at the bottom.
findings.fix: Reads as the house style's vignette edge: the lake fades into the paper. Not worth a redraw.

findings.problem: The shipwright at left, bent over the timber on trestles, pushes an axe along the beam like a plane, its head at the far end; an axe is swung, not pushed.
findings.fix: On the shipwright at the left, bent over the long timber on trestles, replace the axe he holds with a two-handled drawknife like the one the front shipwright uses: a straight blade lying across the timber with a wooden handle at each end, one handle in each of his hands. Change nothing else.

findings.problem: The sealed tablet in its clay envelope reads more like a small decorated cylindrical jar.
findings.fix: A small held object; the card reads as a running messenger. Not worth a redraw.

findings.problem: The share is a black curved iron mouldboard blade, a much later plough; a Sumerian ard (4000–3000 BCE) has a narrow pointed wooden share.
findings.fix: Replace the black curved metal blade at the foot of the plough with a narrow, pointed wooden share in the same brown wood as the frame, angled forward and down with its tip sunk into the furrowed soil. Change nothing else.

findings.problem: The dotted course line runs from the ship to a corner star of the Little Dipper's bowl; Polaris is the star at the tip of its handle, and nothing marks it.
findings.fix: Remove the dotted line between the ship's sail and the constellation. Draw a new dotted line in the same small dots arcing from just above the ship's sail up to the star at the left end of the constellation's handle, and make that one star a larger, bright four-pointed star like the others in the sky. Change nothing else.

findings.problem: In both skiffs the rowers still sit facing the bow (the end with the eye), with their oar blades trailing behind them; oarsmen sit facing the stern and pull.
findings.fix: Turning figures round is beyond the editor: rewrite the prompt to say which way the rowers face and redraw.

findings.problem: The rowers face the bow (push-rowing) although the prompt asked for them to face the stern.
findings.fix: Redraw used. Seated push-rowing facing forward is a real Mediterranean technique for small skiffs, and the generator draws it this way every time.
